openQuestions.q: Should CHK-002 explicitly extend the carried test with the promised reviewer-evidence-bytes and git-state invariance assertion, or should its adversarial verification intent be narrowed?
openQuestions.evidence: CHK-002 requires selector GREEN adversarial: done_prepare parity evaluation leaves reviewer evidence and git state unchanged, and plan.md promises that assertion, but the reviewed test referenced by red-evidence.json contains neither that selector nor pre/post byte or git-state comparison; CHK-001 simultaneously says to materialize it without changing behavioral assertions.
openQuestions.resolution: The Story will preserve both reviewed RED parity assertions but extend the committed test with explicit before/after reviewer-evidence byte comparison and git-status equality. The revised CHK-001 exclusion and plan clarify that 'unchanged' applies to the two RED assertions, not to omission of the required read-only acceptance check.

openQuestions.q: Is CHK-003 required to prevent omission of any future DONE predicate, or only to lock the two known predicates in this Story?
openQuestions.evidence: scope-boundary.json promises that future DONE predicate additions cannot silently bypass done_prepare, but plan.md only registers and tests the two known predicates. Removing either known row will fail, while adding a third independent predicate only to machine.ts is not shown to fail any planned check. Either define a general inventory/shared-aggregate parity mechanism and mutation test, or narrow the promise to these two predicates.
